name: FUFOX (Grothey weekly)

drugs.name: OXALIplatin
drugs.notes: DeVita 12th ed., line 123742: 'Oxaliplatin 50 mg/m2 over 2 hr, followed by LV 500 mg/m2, followed by 5-FU 2,000 mg/m2 over 24 hr, weekly for 5 wk, repeated every 6 wk.' Given first in sequence. Tall man per NCCN Templates Appendix G.

drugs.name: Leucovorin
drugs.notes: DeVita 12th ed., line 123742-123743: 'followed by LV 500 mg/m2'. No range printed. Given second, immediately after oxaliplatin.

drugs.name: 5-Fluorouracil
drugs.notes: DeVita 12th ed., line 123743: 'followed by 5-FU 2,000 mg/m2 over 24 hr, weekly for 5 wk, repeated every 6 wk.' No range printed. Given last, as a 24-hr continuous infusion.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: per moderate emetic risk tier (oxaliplatin), before chemotherapy administration; see supportiveCare

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: moderate emetic risk tier (driven by oxaliplatin) per NCCN Templates Appendix D categories (5-FU/leucovorin alone are low/minimal risk; oxaliplatin sets the regimen tier); prophylaxis on day of treatment per NCCN Antiemesis guideline

G-CSF: not routinely indicated. Weekly oxaliplatin/5-FU/LV regimens are not called out as High or Intermediate febrile-neutropenia risk in NCCN Templates Appendix C; per Appendix C, regimens without a specific FN risk designation default to physician judgment on CSF support

Administration sequence per source: oxaliplatin over 2 hr, followed by leucovorin, followed by 5-FU infusion over 24 hr (NCCN Templates Appendix F: no single agreed evidence-based sequence exists, but this is the order printed in the source regimen)

doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Protocol-specific delay/reduce criteria may apply; physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

provenanceNote: Textbook-grounded draft; NCCN per-disease template, clinical (StewardMD) review, and hospital/institutional approval pending.
